questions.question: What is the difference between top-down and bottom-up tasking approaches in Project Management?

options.text: Top-down focuses on small tasks first; bottom-up focuses on phases first
Top-down focuses on high-level tasks and phases first; bottom-up focuses on estimating small tasks first then aggregating upward
Top-down is for waterfall projects; bottom-up is for agile projects
There is no difference between the two approaches

explanation.correct: Top-down (strategic) tasking means planning high-level tasks and phases first, then breaking down into smaller units. Bottom-up (tactical) tasking means planning small individual units of work first, then building up to larger phases. Bottom-up is the recommended approach for the Project Management application.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is reversed; top-down focuses on phases first, bottom-up on small tasks first
Both approaches can be used with waterfall or agile methodologies
There are significant differences between the two approaches

source.excerpt: Top-down (strategic) tasking means that you plan high-level tasks first, then break down the work into smaller units. Bottom-up (tactical) tasking means that you plan small, individual units of work.

questions.question: What is a milestone in ServiceNow Project Management?

options.text: A project task with a duration of 7 days
A project task with a duration of zero (0)
A budget checkpoint in a project
A required approval gate

explanation.correct: A milestone is a project task with a duration of zero (0). Milestones are used to indicate important dates in a project and can have dependencies with other tasks so that tasks do not start until a milestone has been reached.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A milestone has zero duration, not 7 days
Milestones mark key dates, not budget checkpoints specifically
While milestones can represent approval points, they are defined as zero-duration tasks

source.excerpt: A milestone is a project task with a duration of 0. Use milestones to indicate important dates in a project.

questions.question: What types of task dependencies are supported in ServiceNow Project Management? (Choose FOUR)

options.text: Finish-to-start
Start-to-start
Start-to-finish
Finish-to-finish
Parallel-to-parallel
Sequential-to-concurrent

explanation.correct: ServiceNow Project Management supports four types of task dependencies: Finish-to-start (task must not start until predecessor finishes), Start-to-start (successor must not start until predecessor starts), Start-to-finish (successor must not finish until predecessor starts), and Finish-to-finish (task must not finish until another task finishes).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Parallel-to-parallel is not a supported dependency type
Sequential-to-concurrent is not a supported dependency type

source.excerpt: Finish-to-start dependency, Start-to-start dependency, Start-to-finish dependency, Finish-to-finish dependency.

questions.question: What is a baseline in Project Management?

options.text: The minimum budget required for a project
A snapshot of current planned start and end dates at the time the baseline was created
The first task in a project
The default settings for all projects

explanation.correct: A baseline is a snapshot of the current planned start and end dates at the time the baseline was created for each task. A line appears under each task on the Gantt chart showing the original planned dates, shifted left or right depending on whether tasks started early or late.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A baseline is a date snapshot, not a budget requirement
A baseline captures planned dates across all tasks, not just the first task
A baseline is project-specific, not default settings for all projects

source.excerpt: A baseline is a snapshot of the current planned start and end dates at the time the baseline was created for each task.

questions.question: What happens when you change a project's state to 'Work in Progress'?

options.text: All project tasks are automatically assigned
The Actual start date of the project changes to the planned start date
The project is locked from further changes
All resources are automatically allocated

explanation.correct: When you change the State field on the Project form to Work in Progress, the Actual start date of the project changes to the planned start date. This marks the official start of project execution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Tasks are not automatically assigned when changing to Work in Progress
The project can still be modified while in Work in Progress state
Resource allocation is done through Resource Management, not automatically on state change

source.excerpt: When you change the State field on the Project form to Work in Progress, the Actual start date of the project changes to the planned start date.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about linking change requests to project tasks?

options.text: A project task link record is created when linking a change request
A project task can have both task link records and child project tasks
Multiple change requests can be linked to a single project task
The project task link record is read only

explanation.correct: A project task cannot have both task link records and child project tasks. When a project task is linked to a change request, you cannot create child tasks for that project task. Likewise, when a project task has child tasks, you cannot link the parent project task to a change record.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A project task link record is indeed created when linking a change request
You can link multiple change requests to a single project task
The project task link record is read only

source.excerpt: A project task cannot have both task link records and child project tasks.

questions.question: What is lag time in project task dependencies?

options.text: The time a task is behind schedule
A manually specified time break between predecessor and successor tasks
The delay in system response time
The time between project approval and start

explanation.correct: Lag time is a manually specified time break between predecessor and successor tasks. It allows you to add a deliberate delay or gap between dependent tasks in your project schedule.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Task delay is schedule variance, not lag time
System response time is unrelated to project lag time
Lag time is between tasks, not between approval and project start

source.excerpt: Lag time - A manually specified time break between predecessor and successor tasks.

questions.question: What happens when a project is closed? (Choose THREE)

options.text: The Project Management application calculates actual values like Actual duration
All project records are automatically deleted
You can cancel future resource plans for the project
The project can be used as a template for future projects if successful
All project tasks are automatically reopened

explanation.correct: When a project is closed (state set to Closed complete), the application calculates actual values like Actual duration. You can cancel future resource plans and complete allocated resource plans. If successful, the project can be copied and used as a template for future projects.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Project records are not deleted when closed; they are retained for historical analysis
Closing a project does not reopen tasks; it finalizes them

source.excerpt: When a project is in the closed state, the Project Management application calculates actual values. You can cancel the future resource plans. If the project was successful, make a copy of it.

questions.question: What is a rollup task in Project Management?

options.text: A task that must be completed before project closure
Another term for a parent task that aggregates child task values
A task that rolls over to the next sprint
A recurring task that repeats weekly

explanation.correct: A rollup task is another term for a parent task in the context of aggregating child task items such as effort or resources into a larger parent task calculation. All fields on rollup task forms are read-only because they are calculated from child tasks.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A rollup task is not specifically related to project closure
Rolling over to next sprint is different from rollup aggregation
A rollup task is not a recurring task

source.excerpt: Rollup task - Another term for a parent task in the context of aggregating child task items, such as effort or resources, into a larger parent task calculation.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about state changes in Project Management is TRUE?

I. State changes roll down from the project to project tasks.
II. State changes roll down from parent tasks to child tasks.
III. State changes roll up from child tasks to parent tasks.
IV. State changes in projects have no effect on tasks.

options.text: I and II only
III and IV only
I, II, and III
I only

explanation.correct: State changes roll down from the project to project tasks, and from parent tasks to child tasks. This is in contrast to value calculations which roll up from child tasks to parent tasks.

wrongAnswers.explanation: State changes roll down, not up. Statement IV is also false
Statement III is about value calculations, not state changes
Statement II is also true; state changes roll down from parent to child tasks

source.excerpt: Roll down - State changes roll down from the project to project tasks, and from parent tasks to child tasks.

questions.question: Which tasking approach is recommended for the Project Management application?

options.text: Top-down tasking
Bottom-up tasking
Hybrid tasking
Parallel tasking

explanation.correct: Bottom-up tasking is the recommended approach for the Project Management application. It involves planning small, individual units of work first, then building up to larger phases. The application better supports this approach through rollup calculations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While supported, top-down is not the recommended approach for this application
Hybrid tasking is not specifically mentioned as a recommended approach
Parallel tasking is not a documented tasking approach

source.excerpt: It is the recommended approach for the Project Management application.

questions.question: What are the steps to create a waterfall phase in the project workbench? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Click the Add phase icon
Select Waterfall from the Phase Type choice list
Create a new project first
Import phases from a template

explanation.correct: To create a waterfall phase for a project, click the Add phase icon and select Waterfall from the Phase Type choice list. This creates a waterfall phase within the existing project.

wrongAnswers.explanation: You add phases to an existing project, not create a new one
Phases are created directly, not imported from templates for this action

source.excerpt: Click the Add phase icon and select Waterfall from the Phase Type choice list.

questions.question: What constraint applies to child tasks regarding their parent task start date?

options.text: Child task start dates must occur at least 7 days after the parent task start date
Child task start dates cannot occur before the start date of the parent task
Child tasks have no relationship to parent task dates
Child task start dates must match the parent task start date exactly

explanation.correct: Child task start dates cannot occur before the start date of the parent task. This ensures that child tasks are properly contained within their parent task's timeframe.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no 7-day requirement; child tasks just cannot start before the parent
Child tasks do have a relationship to parent task dates
Child tasks can start on or after the parent start date, not necessarily exactly on it

source.excerpt: Child task - A project task that is a subset of a larger task. Child task start dates cannot occur before the start date of the parent task.

questions.question: How many relationships can exist between two tasks in Project Management?

options.text: Unlimited relationships
Up to four relationships
Only one relationship
At least two relationships

explanation.correct: Only one relationship can exist between two tasks. This ensures clarity in the dependency structure and prevents conflicting constraints between task pairs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is a limit of one relationship between any two tasks
While there are four types of dependencies, only one can exist between two tasks
There is a maximum of one relationship, not a minimum of two

source.excerpt: Note: Only one relationship can exist between two tasks.

questions.question: What prerequisites must be met before creating agile phases in a project workbench? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Project Portfolio Management must be installed
Agile Development 2.0 must be installed
Resource Management Workspace must be activated
Financial Management must be configured

explanation.correct: The Agile phase type option appears only when both the Project Portfolio Management and Agile Development 2.0 applications are installed. These are the prerequisites for creating agile phases in the project workbench.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Resource Management Workspace is not required for agile phase creation
Financial Management is not a prerequisite for agile phases

source.excerpt: This option appears only when both the Project Portfolio Management and Agile Development 2.0 applications are installed.

questions.question: What is a portfolio in ServiceNow Project Management?

options.text: A collection of documents related to a project
A group of related projects
A list of available resources
A report showing project status

explanation.correct: A portfolio is a group of related projects. The Project Management application provides a useful portfolio view that makes it easy to report on the status of all projects in a portfolio. Portfolios also include demands.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A portfolio contains projects and demands, not just documents
Resource lists are managed in Resource Management, not portfolios
Reports are generated from portfolios, but a portfolio is the collection of projects

source.excerpt: A portfolio is a group of related projects.

questions.question: When using top-down tasking, what happens if you create a task with a later start-on date than the project start date?

options.text: The task is automatically rejected
The project shifts to the later start date
The task start date is changed to match the project
An error message is displayed

explanation.correct: When using top-down tasking, creating a task under a project with a start-on date later than the project start date causes the project to shift to the later start date. This is why caution is needed when creating tasks for top-down tasking.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The task is not rejected; the project dates shift
The project adjusts to the task, not the other way around
No error is displayed; the system adjusts the project dates

source.excerpt: Creating a task under a project that has a start-on date later than the start date of the project, the project shifts to the later start date.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a question to consider when planning a project in ServiceNow?

options.text: Do you want a top-down or bottom-up approach to tasking?
What types of dependencies do the tasks have with other tasks?
What social media platforms will be used to promote the project?
Can milestones and project baselines help manage the project?

explanation.correct: Social media promotion is not part of the project planning considerations in ServiceNow. The documentation recommends considering tasking approach, dependencies, milestones and baselines, skills and resources, and tracking project costs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Tasking approach is a key planning consideration
Task dependencies are an important planning consideration
Milestones and baselines are recommended planning considerations

source.excerpt: Before creating a project, consider the following questions and issues.
